idea: AgentSIM's working Java Card applet uses P-256 elliptic-curve cryptography (ECC) to control what a personal NEAR AI agent can spend. The applet generates the owner's signing key and signs spending grants and revocations. Its APDU interface has no private-key export command. Phone-based control requires a compatible, provisioned SIM or eSIM and authorized phone access, without a separate consumer signing device. You choose the recipient, per-payment limit, total budget and expiry, and can revoke future spending. The Rust NEAR vault verifies the owner's P-256 permissions. A separate Ed25519 session key signs each agent spend and a restricted Ed25519 relayer submits it. In our live hardware test, the physical SIM supported P-256 ECC and signed successfully with ECDSA. The November 15 recorded payment signed the owner grant on the physical SIM over PC/SC and stores the applet AID and the pinned key; the earlier control ran in the emulator. A live NEAR AI response supplied the amount and recipient for a local NEAR run that transferred 0.001 test NEAR and completed its callback. Four forbidden relay actions, overspending and a post-revocation payment were rejected. The phone approval interface has not shipped. The first commercial SIM dates to 1991. GSMA's 2026 figures are 8.8 billion wireless connections and 5.8 billion unique subscribers, not a count of compatible cards. Website: https://agentsimnear.xyz/.
